title: Measuring the Share of the Season Still to Come on a Granite Ridge Season Pass
content:
The share of the season still to come on a Granite Ridge Season Pass Programme pass record is measured as follows.

**First.** Where the tier admits the holder on fewer days than a quarter — one day in 4 — of the days the season runs, the share still to come is the whole, a share of 1. A pass sold as a block of days is not used up by the calendar, and what the holder has taken is settled by the day use deduction rather than by the time remaining.

**Second.** Where the tier admits the holder on at least a quarter of the days the season runs and the pass became scannable after the day the season opened, the share still to come is the days from the handling date to the season's last day set against the days from the day the pass became scannable to the season's last day, so that only the part of the season the holder actually had is counted.

**Otherwise.** In any other case the share is not measured differently by this rule.

### The three measures

| Operating days the tier admits the holder on, against the days the season runs | The day the pass became scannable | The share still to come |
| --- | --- | --- |
| fewer than one day in 4 | any | the whole, a share of 1 |
| at least one day in 4 | after the day the season opened | the days still to come set against the days from the day the pass became scannable to the season's last day |
| at least one day in 4 | on or before the day the season opened | not measured differently by this rule |

### Worked on hypothetical figures

A season running from 2026-11-20 to 2027-04-18 is 149 days, so a quarter of it is passed at 38 operating days.

A tier admitting the holder on 4 days falls below that mark, so the share still to come is the whole whatever the handling date.

A tier admitting the holder on 150 days does not, and on a pass that became scannable on 20 December the days from that day to 2027-04-18 number 119. With 60 days still to come on the handling date, the share is 60 set against 119.
